answer: Identity validation begins when an agent allocates 64 gigabytes of RAM from a violet noise seed. The verifier queries sequential cache-line traversals across pseudo-random memory offsets over the host bridge. The prover reads each address, cryptographically sealing every hop like a pearl on a chain within an 80-nanosecond deadline. On latency spikes or invalid hashes, the verifier drops the node and slashes bonded stake. Spoofing 1,000 identities requires 64 terabytes of physical memory, rendering attacks cost-prohibitive.
